caveats: 12000 x 7 is small enough that DESeq2 runs in seconds; do not over-allocate resources

steps.question: Which genes are differentially expressed between treated and control liver samples given 3 replicates per group in counts.csv (12000 genes x 7 samples) and metadata.csv (6 samples x condition)?
acceptance_criteria: Sample identifiers in counts.csv are matched against metadata.csv; any mismatch (e.g. the 7th count column with no metadata row) is explicitly reported and either resolved or that sample is excluded with justification — never silently dropped without a note
Raw counts are modeled with DESeq2 (design ~ condition), size factors estimated via median-of-ratios, and Wald tests run for treated vs control
Log2 fold changes are shrunk (apeglm or ashr) before reporting, given the n=3-per-group dispersion estimation limits
Output table includes gene symbol, baseMean, log2FoldChange, shrunken LFC, p-value, and BH-adjusted p-value (padj) for all tested genes
A results table filtered at padj < 0.05 (and/or a stated |log2FC| threshold) is produced as the DE gene list
PCA or sample-distance plot on variance-stabilized counts is generated to visually confirm treated/control separation and flag any outlier sample before trusting the DE call

steps.name: Power and reliability assessment for the n=3-per-group DE call
caveats: Do not present a post-hoc power number as if it were a pre-registered power calculation — frame it as a diagnostic on the achieved data, not a guarantee

Leave-one-out stability checks with n=3 per group are themselves low-powered (each fold uses only 2 vs 3 samples) — report this as a qualitative stability signal, not a robust cross-validation estimate
steps.question: How much statistical confidence does the 3-vs-3 unpaired design actually support for the DE genes identified in T1S1, and what fold-change/effect sizes would this design reliably detect?
acceptance_criteria: Report the empirical distribution of per-gene dispersion estimates from the DESeq2 fit and compare pre- vs post-shrinkage dispersion to characterize estimation noise at n=3

Estimate approximate statistical power for detecting a range of fold changes (e.g. 1.5x, 2x, 4x) at the observed mean dispersion and library sizes, using a negative-binomial power calculation or simulation-based approach appropriate for n=3 per group

State explicitly the minimum detectable effect size at 80% power given the observed count depth and dispersion, and contrast that against the log2FoldChange values actually observed in the T1S1 results

Quantify sensitivity of the DE gene list to method choice: report how the significant gene count changes under an alternative multiple-testing correction (e.g. independent filtering off vs on) or under leave-one-out resampling of the 3 replicates, as a concrete stability check rather than a single fixed list
Deliver a plain-language confidence statement: what can and cannot be concluded from 3 replicates per group, tied to the actual numbers computed (not generic boilerplate)

steps.name: Pathway enrichment of the DE gene list against WikiPathways (human)
caveats: Confirm the WikiPathways human GMT file is present before running (staged at the human WikiPathways reference in this environment); if absent for any reason, report the gap rather than substituting a mouse/rat gene set
Gene symbol case/synonym mismatches between the counts.csv gene column and the GMT HGNC symbols should be checked and reported, not silently dropped without a count of unmapped genes
steps.question: Which WikiPathways pathways are over-represented among the genes differentially expressed between treated and control liver samples?
acceptance_criteria: Use the WikiPathways human gene set collection (HGNC symbols) staged in the environment for over-representation or GSEA-style analysis
Input is the padj<0.05 DE gene list from T1S1 (over-representation) and/or the full ranked gene list by shrunken log2FoldChange (for GSEA/fgsea), state which was used
Report pathway name, WikiPathways ID, gene overlap count, and adjusted enrichment p-value (BH or FDR) for all pathways passing significance

If the DE gene list is very short (a real possibility at n=3 per group), report this explicitly rather than forcing enrichment on an underpowered list, and note the resulting enrichment results should be read as exploratory

plan.title: Liver treated vs control DE with power caveats
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is a bulk RNA-seq liver drug-treatment study with raw Salmon gene-level counts (12000 genes x 7 samples in counts.csv, 6 annotated samples in metadata.csv — note the count matrix has 7 columns but metadata has only 6 rows, so the DE step must reconcile sample naming before fitting). Design is 3 treated vs 3 control, unpaired, single batch. With n=3/group the standard approach is DESeq2's negative-binomial GLM with Wald tests, which is appropriate for raw counts and handles the modest library-size and dispersion variability expected at this replicate depth; but n=3 gives limited power to estimate per-gene dispersion, so shrinkage (apeglm/ashr) on log2FoldChange is necessary rather than optional, and the plan explicitly reports power limitations rather than treating the result as a definitive DE list. After DE, the significant gene list is enriched against WikiPathways human pathways to give biological context to what the design can support, and a dedicated statistical step quantifies achieved power/precision at n=3 so the user gets an honest confidence statement alongside the DE table.
